title: Cold rebuild: the autocomplete trie
summary: Rebuild the trie with top-k suggestions at every node from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **a trie with top-k suggestions** in *Design search autocomplete*. Now
write it again from an **empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly
the ones you passed the first time.
Why: "store the answer at each node" is an idea you will reuse (precomputed timelines, rollups, materialised
views). Rebuilding it cold shows whether you own it. If you get stuck, go back to the lesson and try again
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Your trie keeps the top 5 at each node and counts only grow. A query outside a node's top 5 gets more searches. What must `Add` do at that node?
options: Insert that query into the node's list, re-sort and trim back to 5; no other query can need to come back
Rebuild the node's list from its whole subtree
Nothing: lists are only rebuilt in the nightly job
Clear the list so the next lookup recomputes it
steps.explain: Only that one query's total changed, and it only went up. Anything previously trimmed was beaten by queries whose totals can only have grown, so it cannot belong back.

steps.prompt: Why is suggestion traffic a good fit for CDN caching?
options: The answer for a prefix is the same for everyone in a language and region, and short prefixes are most of the traffic
CDNs can run trie lookups at the edge
steps.explain: A few minutes of edge caching on `GET /suggest?q=...&lang=...` removes most of the load while keeping results fresh enough.

steps.title: Cold rebuild: Autocomplete
prompt: - `void Add(string query, long count)`: adds to the query's total.
- `List<string> Suggest(string prefix)`: up to `k` queries starting with `prefix`, highest total first, ties in
ordinal order; an unknown prefix gives an empty list and `""` matches everything.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
